statement: A tree is given as: a line with n, then a line of n level-order entries where -1 marks an absent child; each placed node consumes the next two entries as its left and right children. Print the postorder traversal - the whole left subtree, then the whole right subtree, then the root - as space-separated values. Postorder finishes both children before their parent, making it the only safe order for jobs where a node needs its children's results first, like subtree sizes or safe deletion.
constraints: Node values are positive; -1 marks an absent child.

example.why: Leaves 4 and 5 report before their parent 2; the right subtree 3 follows; the root 1 is last.

hint: Recurse left, recurse right, visit - the root is always the final value printed.
mistake: Expecting postorder to read bottom level first across the tree; it is per-subtree, left before right.
